messages.author: 290a5aa21708d167
messages.subject: bootstrap ci for mediation
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm trying to obtain bootstrap CIs for a simple mediation model with lavaan, and am wondering what is the difference between using parameterEstimates() vs. bootstrapLavaan().
What is the default number of bootstrap reps for boot.ci.type=" " in parameterEstimates()?

When I run the following code, why do I get different bootstrap percentile CIs? Is my assumption that they should be the same incorrect?

N <- 50
a <- .35
b <- .59
c <- .7
x <- rnorm(N)
dat <- data.frame(x,m,y)

m1 <-'y ~ c*x + b*m
      m ~ a*x
      ab := a*b
      total: = c +(a*b)'
fit1 <- sem(m1, data=dat) 

parameterEstimates(fit1, boot.ci.type="perc")

#    lhs op     rhs label   est    se     z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
#1     y  ~       x     c 0.756 0.138 5.473  0.000    0.485    1.027
#2     y  ~       m     b 0.747 0.115 6.500  0.000    0.522    0.973
#3     m  ~       x     a 0.277 0.165 1.673  0.094   -0.048    0.601
#4     y ~~       y       0.694 0.139 5.000  0.000    0.422    0.966
#5     m ~~       m       1.050 0.210 5.000  0.000    0.638    1.462
#6     x ~~       x       0.768 0.000    NA     NA    0.768    0.768
#7    ab :=     a*b    ab 0.207 0.128 1.620  0.105   -0.043    0.457
#8 total := c+(a*b) total 0.963 0.183 5.273  0.000    0.605    1.321

boot.reps <- bootstrapLavaan(fit1, R=1000)
ab.reps <- boot.reps[,2]*boot.reps[,3]
boot.95lb <- ab.reps[order(ab.reps)][25]
boot.95ub <- ab.reps[order(ab.reps)][975]

boot.95lb
# -0.0129184
boot.95ub
# 0.4101657

Thanks,

Jolynn

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: bootstrap ci for mediation
parts: When I run the following code, why do I get different bootstrap percentile CIs? Is my assumption that they should be the same incorrect?

I think your syntax example skips the step where m and y are generated.  Do you get the same results if you set the same RNG seed before calling parameterEstimates and bootstrapLavaan?
